newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen steady after Wednesday loss.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen steady after Wednesday loss.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open steady Thursday from yesterday's settlement after Wednesday's losses tied to easing cash market prices in the western U.S., market sources said.

In over-the-counter trading, September Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $30.80-31.10 a megawatt hour (MWh) against Wednesday's $30.87 after traded as high as $31.85. September California-Oregon Border (COB) was talked at $23.00-23.20 versus yesterday's close at $23.29.
Day-head firm, peak power prices at PV were offered at $60.00 a MWh after breaking above $100 yestersday, while those at COB dropped $10.00 to $30.00-35.00.
Spot power business in the West was expected to be light today due to an industry conference in Vancouver today, market sources noted.
California and the interior section of the West will likely brace for another day of scorching heat and record power demand.
Both Pacific Gas & Electric Co and Southern California Edison Co posted peak power demand records Wednesday due to soaring air-conditioning usage.
In the latest six to 10 day forecasts, the West was expected to experience a cooling trends, moderating toward more seasonal summer temperatures.
"It supposed to get a little cooler this weekend, but it's not going to put a lot of pressure on the market," a New York futures broker said.

Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said Wednesday operating transmission capacity on the AC portion of the Pacific Intertie system will hold at 3,450 megawatt (MW), although the operating limit of AC part of the system was increased to 3,800 MW.
Electricity output from the 1,221 MW Palo Verde nuclear power unit 3 in Wintersburg, Ariz., continued to hold at 90 percent power early Thursday for repairs to a condensate pump.
The adjacent 1,221 MW Palo Verde nuclear power unit 2 was also operating at 90 percent of capacity as of early Thursday as the unit coasts down to a scheduled refueling outage September 6.
